title: Latency-aware kernel tuner and regression mitigation for FlashAttention v3
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: reduce 95th-percentile small-batch decode latency regressions observed when routing to FlashAttention v3 while preserving macro throughput improvements. This ticket contains the experimentation log, tuning knobs, and an actionable mitigation (tuner + staged rollout) that integrates with the runtime kernel selector and prefill/decode scheduler.

Background: After onboarding FA v3 on a subset of instances we saw ~12-20% tail latency regressions for short prompt + short decode requests (<=64 tokens) under light to medium concurrency. Investigation pointed at a combination of microtiling differences in v3 kernels and an interaction with the runtime's prefill-to-decode handoff timing when ongoing batches are sparse. The goal is to create a latency-aware tuner that (1) adjusts kernel selection thresholds based on per-shape latency curves, (2) coordinates with prefill/decode scheduling to avoid decode-start jitter, and (3) provides safe fallback to FA v2 for affected shapes.
acceptance_criteria: 95th-percentile latency for small-batch decode (<=64 tokens) returns to within 5% of baseline (v2) on canary clusters
End-to-end rollout plan documented and automated via canary flags in the runtime
Kernel selector exposes a tunable latency threshold and shape-based override with runtime telemetry to validate decisions
Automated regression test added to perf-rolling-evals comparing v2/v3 on representative shape matrix
Fallback path to v2 triggers within 30s for sustained latency regressions and emits alerting telemetry
implementation_notes: Add per-shape latency profiler at kernel-selection time that records P50/P95 and workspace usage for the shape (batch, seq_len_prefill, seq_len_decode)
Introduce 'latency_cost' metric aggregated in the kernel scorer: weighted combination of P95 latency delta and workspace allocation change
Modify selector ranking so shapes with latency_cost > threshold prefer v2 variant unless v3 shows >1.2x throughput advantage for that shape
Update prefill/decode scheduler: ensure decode tasks are scheduled with a jitter-aware handoff when prefill batches are below prefill_batch_min to avoid warmup stalls
Create a canary toggle (runtime flag) enabling latency-aware tuner per deployment ring and add a rollback policy based on alerting signals
Add unit + integration tests for selector decision function and end-to-end microbench harness that replays production shape histogram
test_results: Baseline (v2) canary run: small-batch decode P95 = 38ms (stddev 3.2)
Initial v3 canary: small-batch decode P95 = 46ms (+21% vs v2), observed at low concurrency (1-4 req/s per GPU)
After tuning (latency_cost threshold=0.12): small-batch decode P95 = 40ms (+5% vs v2) on canary cluster; throughput unchanged for long-context workloads
Fallback automation test: sustained P95 > 1.2x baseline for 60s triggered rollback to v2 and opened incident alert as expected
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy latency profiler and telemetry-only kernel scorer on shadow canaries (no routing) for 3 days. 2) Enable latency-aware selection on a 5% canary ring; monitor P95 and error budgets. 3) If P95 delta < +5% for 48h, expand to 25% ring. 4) Automate fallback to v2 when alert conditions met (P95 sustained >1.2x baseline for 60s or workspace OOM rate >0.01%). 5) Full rollout only after 7-day stability window and signoff from SRE and Product. Rollback window and playbook documented in the runtime runbook.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting thresholds to synthetic shapes leads to oscillations in selector decisions. Mitigation: weight decisions by long-running production histogram and add hysteresis (min interval 5 minutes between forced flips).
Risk: Telemetry latency causes delayed detection of regressions. Mitigation: emit immediate local-side alert metrics and short-path notifications to PagerDuty on canary rings.
Risk: Increased code complexity in selector. Mitigation: small incremental feature flags and thorough unit coverage; keep scorer implementation less than 120 lines and documented
